message:
fix(host): the punch trains run beside the directory cycle, not in it (keepalive-r2 FINDING: the same device again within seconds)

작업용2 (report_ka_pc_impl_r1.md FINDING): a lease of the same key right after the last admission was unanswered
("unsupported") until ~30 s had passed. Reproduced in the e2e against the real server.js relay, and read off the
host's own log (kae_relapse5):

- HostAgent::Punch sent its train -- kPunchPackets (25) x kPunchIntervalMs (200 ms) = 5 s -- INSIDE the directory
  cycle, after the heartbeat that returned capabilities. For those 5 s the agent could not act on the next wake: a
  capability minted meanwhile (here the second admission; a second connect alike) waited for the train and the next
  cycle (collected after 5.1 s) while the host refused its Hellos ("hello refused (capability)", throttled in the log)
  and the client gave its Hellos up after ~3 s. The directory's wakes did arrive (dir-punch refreshWasPending=1).
- A wake during work that ran past the interval was not this cycle's cause either; it lingered to the next one.

Now Punch() hands its targets to a punch thread (the same packets and spacing; a target punched again starts its
count over) and returns; the cycle goes straight to its wait and serves the next wake. A wake during overrun work is
the next cycle's cause at once.

e2e --product-client --real-directory --old-host: 78/78 (new: device X through the relay; the same device again at once
after a crash -- 599 ms -- and after a release -- 1596 ms; each its own relay lease). Before: those failed (the third
admission and both re-admissions unanswered for 5 s, collected at 5.06-5.14 s). punch_reply_test 55/55, directory http
contract PASS. The host's directory / punch / standby lines are printed after it stops (HOSTLOG).
